newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's King Hussein visits Israeli families.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's King Hussein visits Israeli families.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein on Sunday clutched the hands of an Israeli mother and father whose daughter was killed by a Jordanian soldier and told them their loss was also his own.

Hussein, on a condolence visit to the Jewish state after seven schoolgirls were shot dead at the Israeli-Jordanian border on Thursday, knelt in the living room of the Fatihi family where relatives sat on the floor in keeping with Jewish tradition during mourning.
"The memory of your daughter will live with me forever. I hope her memory will give you strength," the king told the parents of Sivan Fatihi, who was 13 when she was killed.
"Your loss is my loss, my personal loss," he said.
The monarch, wearing a red Arab keffiyeh headdress, was accompanied by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who translated for the king.
"The peace with Jordan should be the best hope," said Yisrael Fatihi, the father. "I am sure Your Majesty will fight those fanatic extremists."
They showed the king pictures of Sivan, killed while on a school outing with her class at the Island of Peace, a beauty spot on Jordanian soil leased to Israeli farmers under their 1994 peace deal.
The king expressed shame and shock after the attack, which came after Jordanian-Israeli relations had deteriorated sharply over Netanyahu's plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The monarch landed at Tel Aviv airport earlier on Sunday. He was greeted by Netanyahu in their first meeting since a harsh exchange of letters last week over Israeli setttlement plans.

The king has appointed a veteran security official to head investigations into the soldier's motives. Jordanian officials have said the soldier, army driver Sergeant Ahmed Mousa Mustafa al-Daqamsa, acted alone.
